gaps: Plaud Web does not publish a public OpenAPI specification for these workflow endpoints.
Recording organization actions such as rename, folder movement, and local export are useful power-user workflows but are not currently covered by the official public CLI surface.
patterns: Use a user-provided Plaud Web bearer token from the user's own signed-in browser session.
Keep destructive operations out of the first release; no permanent delete command.
Use dry-run support for batch rename workflows.
Never print or persist bearer tokens, cookies, signed audio URLs, or downloaded private audio in manuscripts.

novel_features.name: Batch recording rename
novel_features.description: Rename multiple Plaud recordings from a JSON or CSV mapping after transcription or note synthesis.
novel_features.rationale: Plaud captures recordings quickly, but synthesized knowledge workflows often produce meaningful titles later; pushing those titles back keeps the cloud library searchable.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets agents keep Plaud Web aligned with Obsidian, CRM, and meeting-note systems without manual timestamp cleanup.

novel_features.name: Local audio export
novel_features.description: Resolve a short-lived Plaud audio URL and download the recording to a local file with a safe title-based filename.
novel_features.rationale: The web app exposes temporary audio URLs, but agents need a durable local export primitive for owned recordings.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Supports data portability and downstream transcript, archival, or review workflows.

novel_features.name: Folder organization
novel_features.description: Move one or more recordings into a Plaud folder/tag or back to unfiled.
novel_features.rationale: Folder operations turn Plaud from a timestamp list into an organized source library.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Useful for client calls, event recordings, and presentation-prep batches.
